events.reasoning:
The program has a syntax error that prevents it from running at all. Inside process_feed, the success branch builds HTML with a nested f-string: f'
  • {item["headline"]}
    • ' The replacement fields `{item["link"]}` and `{item["headline"]}` contain backslashes. On Python 3.11 and earlier this raises `SyntaxError: f-string expression part cannot include a backslash` at compile time (the backslash is not removed before the expression is parsed). Even on Python 3.12+, where backslashes in f-string replacement fields were relaxed, the field content `item["link"]` is still not valid Python — the escaped quotes would only be meaningful inside a string literal, not as bare characters in the expression — so it remains an error. Since the file fails to parse, `main()` is never reached and `report.html` is never produced, regardless of the input. Aside from that blocker, the rest of the logic is largely consistent with the task (200 check, dict/`items` check, slicing to first 3, per-feed section ordering, `unavailable` fallback). The only other deviations are minor: it does not verify that `title` is a string or that each item has string `headline`/`link` before emitting them, though missing keys would incidentally be caught by the bare `except` and turn into an `unavailable` section. Those are edge cases; the f-string syntax error is fatal.
